source.file_name: Reputation helps solve the ‘tragedy of the commons’.pdf

paper.title: Reputation helps solve the ‘tragedy of the commons’
paper.research_question: Can reputation from an indirect reciprocity game sustain contributions in a public goods game?
paper.setting: anonymous pseudonymous groups playing public goods and indirect reciprocity games

game_context.endowment: starting account DM 20; per-round PGG endowment not specified in excerpt
game_context.baseline_condition: public goods rounds played without expected later indirect reciprocity/reputation benefits

mechanisms.name: Reputation-coupled indirect reciprocity
mechanisms.summary: Players' giving histories in both the public goods and indirect reciprocity games were publicly displayed before indirect reciprocity decisions, making public-goods contributions valuable for maintaining a good reputation and receiving later help.

actors.decision_maker: public goods contributor and indirect-reciprocity donor
actors.target: potential receiver whose reputation/history is displayed

timing.stage: public goods contribution history is observed during later indirect reciprocity donor decisions
timing.frequency: alternating IR and PGG rounds for first 16 rounds, then terminal PGG rounds

information_structure.anonymity: real identities anonymous; stable pseudonyms used throughout game
public_information: pseudonym-linked history of giving in indirect reciprocity game
pseudonym-linked history of contributions in public goods game
information_structure.history_visibility: receiver's giving history in both games displayed simultaneously for all players in each indirect reciprocity round

action_space_changes.range_or_options: help/give or not help; exact amount not specified in excerpt
contribution amount; exact range not specified in excerpt

payoff_changes.amount_or_formula: costly help creates benefit; exact cost/benefit not specified in excerpt
payoff_changes.condition: donor chooses to help, often favoring good reputation

payoff_changes.amount_or_formula: future expected help depends on observed giving history

state_variables.name: pg_contribution_history
state_variables.update_rule: append each agent's public goods contribution by round under pseudonym

state_variables.name: ir_giving_history
state_variables.update_rule: append each donor's help/giving decisions in indirect reciprocity rounds

state_variables.name: reputation_or_image_score
state_variables.update_rule: derived from visible history of giving in both games

state_variables.name: mean_pgg_contribution
state_variables.update_rule: average public goods contribution per group and round

state_variables.name: profit
state_variables.update_rule: track monetary earnings across both games

prompt_requirements: Tell agents their stable pseudonym and that histories may be visible to others.
Show each potential receiver's prior PGG contributions and IR giving before IR help decisions.
Make clear that PGG contributions can affect later reputation and help received.

metrics.name: mean_public_goods_contribution
metrics.definition: average contribution to the public good by round/group

metrics.name: contribution_decay
metrics.definition: change in PGG contribution over repeated PGG rounds

metrics.name: help_received_by_reputation
metrics.definition: association between visible giving history/image score and probability of receiving IR help

minimal_code_changes: add stable pseudonyms and per-agent history logs
add indirect reciprocity rounds with donor-receiver matching and help action
display target histories in prompts before IR decisions
log reputation/image metrics and help received
optionally add treatment schedule alternating PGG and IR rounds
risks_or_assumptions: exact IR cost-benefit parameters and PGG endowment/multiplier not available in excerpt
LLM agents may require explicit prompt incentives to value future reputation
baseline PGG may not support multi-stage mixed games without extension

directly_implementable: log and display prior PGG contribution history
implementation_order: add per-agent state_memory for pseudonym-linked histories
extend action_space with IR help decisions
extend payoff_function for IR help costs/benefits

experiment_design.baseline_condition: eight public goods rounds before any indirect reciprocity, or terminal PGG rounds after subjects are told no further IR rounds will occur
treatment_conditions: alternating indirect reciprocity and public goods rounds through round 16
unexpected versus announced absence of further indirect reciprocity from round 17
control_variables: same total number of PGG and IR opportunities where applicable

cooperation_outcomes: Alternating public goods with indirect reciprocity maintained unexpectedly high public-goods contributions.
When indirect reciprocity rounds were not expected, public-goods contributions dropped quickly to zero.
Groups starting with eight public goods rounds showed usual decline from round 1 to round 8.
evidence.reported_effect_direction: positive: reputation opportunities increased and sustained cooperation; removing expected reputation benefits reduced cooperation
evidence.reported_effect_size: PGG-first decline: paired t-test round 1 vs 8, n=9 groups, t=6.958, P<0.0001; other exact effect sizes not in excerpt
key_quotes_or_passages: the need to maintain reputation for indirect reciprocity maintains contributions to the public good at an unexpectedly high level
if rounds of indirect reciprocation are not expected, then contributions to the public good drop quickly to zero
each potential receiver’s history of giving both in the indirect reciprocity and the public goods game was displayed simultaneously for all players
players would risk their reputation if they would not cooperate in a public goods game that is alternated with the indirect reciprocity game

uncertainties: Exact per-round PGG endowment, multiplier/MPCR, and IR cost-benefit values are not provided in the excerpt.
Full numerical contribution levels are unavailable from the truncated source text.
